run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:20:58Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by an outage of product-catalog, not by a fault in frontend-proxy itself. The frontend-proxy spans that error are its 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' spans, and its logs show HTTP 500 responses returned 'via_upstream' for product-catalog-dependent routes (/api/products/{id}, /api/checkout) while /api/cart and /api/data still returned 200 [4e50f6ce-4ac1-4945-85c6-2c1cedbabe05-t1:aa71a965-42a1-48bb-853b-0d3d1a6d7f3e]. The frontend's failing client span is grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and detail '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established ... connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080' [795ccc11-31fe-4855-8867-b876a0c523a0-t1:58fa4f0c-8642-4865-b43c-0bb15e2fa76f], and 100.69.9.250:8080 is the product-catalog ClusterIP Service [6ea86d37-e20c-4249-88eb-d1abdd33b8e3-t0:8ada2ee5-1adb-46e5-b160-37eee4fca5e4]. product-catalog has no ready endpoints (Endpoints contain only notReadyAddresses for pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk) [2c007da6-db7e-4073-9926-9a7014ab8419-t1:cfb7419f-33f4-4315-b4a1-527eb4cc3724] because that pod is Pending in ImagePullBackOff pulling quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 (401 UNAUTHORIZED) [c7b7aa46-253f-41a5-a5e4-036a94693e27-t0:29f37a6c-da22-411c-8524-8d62e82bf983]. That invalid image is the image in the pod template of Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog (generation 4, revision 2, no ready/available replicas) [9a50eaca-c6bb-462d-90bc-a15d1da1c178-t0:2655319c-f528-448f-91a3-cfed38e7f25a]; it is the only deployment in the cluster using such an image [fff1809e-2abd-4c1d-8532-a5904d1a5e1a-t1:30979081-eb50-459c-8a6d-2d57903efb73]. Events show the rollout at 01:21:10-01:21:26 replacing the old good ReplicaSet and failing to pull the image, after which product-catalog produced no further spans (newest at 01:21:18) [b7ab5125-2a68-4f94-a2a6-a15546fe4d10-t0:a32ff34e-b8d3-40f4-9851-b93e5f0720c9] [2c007da6-db7e-4073-9926-9a7014ab8419-t0:74d71074-c3d1-432e-a51b-77d5aea49caf]. frontend-proxy, frontend, recommendation and checkout each show their own error spans [5afcbdd3-0099-4dd2-8582-3066b40e3d3d-t0:a9501528-176b-448a-9434-de08d7b7ab67]. Flag-injected faults were not enabled in flagd-config (all flags 'off') and no NetworkPolicy objects were returned, so neither is supported as this cause. What is not verified is who or what changed the Deployment image: the change-history integration is not available in this Run.

claims.text: The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate is defined in the Prometheus rulefiles configmap as: sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR", service_name!~"flagd|load-generator"}[2m])) > 0, i.e. it fires on error-status spans, not on request counts. A lookup of a loaded rule with that exact name in the Prometheus rules API returned nothing (no_data), so only the rule text in the configmap was visible.

frontend-proxy's own error-rate deviation started at ~01:22:30: its STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate (2m rate) was 0.011-0.0167/s between 01:17:00 and 01:22:00, then 2.93/s at 01:22:30, and the two span names 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' together reached ~17.8-18.0/s around 01:32, consistent with the alert annotation value 18.19. The error spans are only 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'.

frontend-proxy access logs at 01:30:38-01:30:39 show HTTP 500 responses 'via_upstream' for GET /api/products/{productId} (e.g. /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM, /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z) and POST /api/checkout, while POST /api/cart and GET /api/data returned 200 in the same seconds.

A frontend trace at 01:26:59 shows the failing call chain visible in that sampled trace: frontend span 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' with rpc.grpc.status_code "14" and error detail '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080 - Local (0.0.0.0:0)', its parent 'executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]' and 'GET /api/products/{productId}'/'GET' with http.status_code 500, and the frontend-proxy 'ingress'/'router frontend egress' spans of the same trace with http.status_code 500.
Service otel-demo/product-catalog has clusterIP 100.69.9.250, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog; this is exactly the address the frontend reported as unreachable.
The Endpoints object for product-catalog contains only notReadyAddresses (100.96.4.116, targetRef pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk) and no ready addresses, so the Service has no serving backend.

Pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk is phase Pending with container 'product-catalog' not ready, restartCount 0, state waiting reason ImagePullBackOff and message 'Back-off pulling image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0": ErrImagePull: ... 401 UNAUTHORIZED'; its owner is ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog has pod-template image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, spec.replicas 1, metadata.generation 4 with observedGeneration 4, revision annotation '2', and status readyReplicas/availableReplicas absent (no ready replica). Its sibling deployments frontend and frontend-proxy are at generation 1 with 1 ready/available replica each.
Among all Deployments in the cluster, only otel-demo/product-catalog has a container image matching 'hello-bench|invalid'; no other workload uses that image.

Events for otel-demo product-catalog: ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966 created pod 8rw7j at 01:21:11, its image pull of quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 failed with 401 UNAUTHORIZED / ErrImagePull / ImagePullBackOff, both the new ReplicaSet and the old product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc were scaled down at 01:21:18 (old pod 7c7f8b68dc-qz548 'Stopping container product-catalog'), and ReplicaSet 56fbb5f966 was scaled back up at 01:21:26 creating pod h9xjk, whose pulls also failed 401 UNAUTHORIZED with further BackOff/ImagePullBackOff at 01:24:36-01:26:41.

The two product-catalog ReplicaSets confirm the rollout: product-catalog-56fbb5f966 was created 01:21:10 with image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 (0 ready), while the earlier product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (created 00:47:37, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) is scaled to 0 replicas. Both are owned by Deployment product-catalog.

The newest product-catalog spans returned for 01:12:00-01:36:11 started at 01:21:18 (the search's source_end_at), and those spans were successful (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct with rpc.grpc.status_code "0"); no product-catalog span later than 01:21:18 was returned, i.e. the service stopped serving after the rollout.

Other services show their own error spans in the same window: frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' 4.14 error-spans/s and 'GET /api/products/{productId}' 4.11/s; recommendation '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' and 'get_product_list' 0.774/s each; checkout 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 0.489/s each; frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'POST /api/checkout' 0.514/s (10m rate at 01:30).

Checked and not elevated at 01:30 (10m error-span rate): payment 0/s, accounting 0/s, ad 0.0018/s, fraud-detection 0.0018/s, currency 0 error-status series; frontend-proxy 11.53/s, frontend 21.97/s, recommendation 1.55/s and checkout 0.98/s were elevated.

Rejected: flagd-driven fault injection into product-catalog. The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) shows every flag at defaultVariant "off", including productCatalogFailure ("off"), adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, so no such setting was in effect when read. (Flag state earlier in the window could not be read.)

Rejected as supported cause: NetworkPolicy blocking of frontend->product-catalog. A cluster-wide read of NetworkPolicy objects returned no items (0 objects processed), so no NetworkPolicy is available to explain the refused/unreachable connection, and the observed cause is the missing ready backend.

The alert's stated start 2026-11-18T01:20:58Z precedes the measured error-rate deviation (~01:22:30) because the rule fires on any rate > 0, and frontend-proxy already carried a small background error-span rate (0.011-0.0167/s at 'ingress' from 01:17 to 01:22); this would make the start time partly a threshold artifact rather than the start of the burst. Not verified from the alert's own evaluation history, which was not available.

Restore the product-catalog Deployment's pod-template image to the previously running ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog (or another pullable valid image), then confirm the ReplicaSet pod becomes Ready and the product-catalog Endpoints gain a ready address; verify registry credentials/authorization for quay.io before any future rollout of that repository.

gaps: What or who changed Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog's pod-template image to quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, and when (generation 4 / revision 2), is unknown: the change_history integration is not available in this Run and no applying object (Job, CronJob, chaos controller) was observed for it.

kube-state-metrics deployment series were not available: a name lookup for kube_deployment.* returned no metric names and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available/ready{deployment="product-catalog"} returned no series, so replica readiness was taken from the Deployment/Pod/Endpoints objects instead.
The frontend container's logs returned no lines for 01:20:00-01:31:00 (0 lines read), so frontend application log output for this window is unknown; its errors were read from spans instead.

The alert evaluation history (when the >0 condition first evaluated true and the exact 2m value at that moment) was not available; the loaded rules API returned nothing for the exact rule name, so the rule was read from the rulefiles ConfigMap.
Trace views are sampled: span counts and the per-operation error rates above describe the returned sample and are not a complete request count or failure rate.

Product-catalog spans after 01:21:18 and product-catalog container logs could not be read (pod has never started), so the state of the old pod at deletion (besides the 'Stopping container product-catalog' event) is unknown.
next_steps: Use cluster audit logs / GitOps or CI history to identify the actor and commit that set Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog's image to quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0.
After reverting the image, verify Service otel-demo/product-catalog Endpoints show a ready address and that frontend /api/products/{productId} and /api/checkout return 200 again.
Check ImagePullSecrets and quay.io repository authorization for otel-demo workloads so invalid/private images fail during rollout validation rather than in production.
